title: Your strengths and your gaps
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What is the one strength you would give away and the weakness you would fix?

Jose asked each person: what is your strength as a leader, and your lack of strength? One student said empathy is a strength and the frequency of communication is a weakness. Another said adaptability and situational awareness.

Jose said that he asked this because we need to analyze: am I a back-end person who keeps the data under control, or a front-end person who can sit with someone and make an emotional and rational connection?

Jose said he can talk about his weaknesses more easily than his strengths. He said he can switch from the empathetic, servant leader to just get this done and become insensitive, and that he has a tendency to switch off while someone talks. Every day he reminds himself to be a better listener.

He said that he focuses on strategy and talks little about operations, so he puts people in place for the day-to-day who remind him of the schedule and milestones. He said he struggles with administrative tasks.
Name your strength and your weakness, and who covers the gap.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your strength as a leader.
Write whether you are back end or front end.
Write the one habit that would help your weakness.

check.q: What did Jose ask each person?
choices: Their strength and their lack of strength

check.q: What did Jose say he does about day-to-day operations?
choices: Puts people in place for them

check.q: What did Jose say he reminds himself to be?

recap: Know your strength and your gap. Put someone in the gap.
